title: Digit reversal — 14 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Digit reversal. 14 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/reversal.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 8 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 6 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). One further declaration closes by rfl, checked by evaluation, and is not included here, by design. Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 3 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 38 pairs; the theorems fall into 5 strands, the largest of 10. Most binding: reverseNum (9), digitSum (2), isPrime (2). 3 theorems name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: z9plus.lean. Checking this cluster needs 1 file: src/proof/reversal.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 14 sealed receipts fold to f7d572e9-6010-899d-912e-778ba70de9a0. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (5, 4, 1, 6, 7, 5, 6). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: rights.lean (3 observed, 1.08 expected, lift 2.77), demand2.lean (3 observed, 1.49 expected, lift 2.02), coin.lean (3 observed, 1.62 expected, lift 1.85). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.77 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 60.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.09; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.53. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 8abd3e4f535b (2026-09-15), over 726 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. Digit reversal and digit sums; casting out nines, in use by the 12th century. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. reversal_preserves_digit_sum — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => digitSum (reverseNum n) == digitSum n) record
  2. digital_root_is_invariant_under_reversal — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => (reverseNum n) % 9 == n % 9) record
  3. the_ledger_reversal_cases — (reverseNum 12) % 9 == 12 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 45) % 9 == 45 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 123) % 9 == 123 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 1234) % 9 == 1234 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 4321) % 9 == 4321 % 9 ∧ (reverseNum 9080) % 9 == 9080 % 9 record
  4. reversal_is_not_the_identity — ¬ ((List.range' 10 90).all (fun n => reverseNum n == n)) record
  5. palindromes_are_the_fixed_points — ((List.range' 10 90).filter (fun n => reverseNum n == n)).length = 9 record
  6. emirps_exist_below_one_hundred — ((List.range' 10 90).filter (fun n => isPrime n && isPrime (reverseNum n) && reverseNum n != n)).length > 0 record
  7. reversal_does_not_preserve_primality — ¬ ((List.range' 10 90).all (fun n => isPrime n == isPrime (reverseNum n))) record
  8. reversal_is_involutive_exactly_off_the_trailing_zeros — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => (reverseNum (reverseNum n) == n) == (n % 10 != 0)) record
  9. foldl_add_start — ∀ (l : List Nat) (a : Nat), l.foldl (· + ·) a = a + l.foldl (· + ·) 0 record
  10. the_digits_sum_to_the_number_mod_nine_when_the_fuel_covers_them — ∀ f n : Nat, n < 10 ^ f → (digitsF f n).foldl (· + ·) 0 % 9 = n % 9 record
  11. a_number_is_below_ten_to_its_own_successor — ∀ n : Nat, n < 10 ^ (n + 1) record
  12. the_digit_sum_has_the_residue_of_the_number_mod_nine_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, digitSum n % 9 = n % 9 record
  13. folding_by_ten_keeps_the_residue_of_the_digit_sum — ∀ (l : List Nat) (a : Nat), (l.foldl (fun a d => a * 10 + d) a) % 9 = (a + l.foldl (· + ·) 0) % 9 record
  14. reversal_keeps_the_residue_mod_nine_for_every_n — ∀ n : Nat, reverseNum n % 9 = n % 9 record
